Operators on Z3 expressions

Source: R/operators.R
z3_operators.Rd

Arithmetic, comparison and logical operators build new symbolic expressions instead of computing R values.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'z3_expr'
Ops(e1, e2)

Arguments

e1, e2

z3_expr objects or R scalars.

Value

A z3_expr.

Details

OperatorInt / RealBoolbit-vector
+, -, *arithmeticerrormodular arithmetic
/exact real divisionerrorerror, see z3_bvudiv()
^powererrorerror
%/%, %%Int only: SMT-LIB div, moderrorerror
==, !=equationequivalenceequation
<, <=, >, >=comparisonerrorerror, see z3_bvult()
&, \|, !errorand, or, notbitwise and, or, not

Int and Real operands can be mixed; the Int operand is converted to Real exactly. Every other combination of sorts is an error: Booleans are not numbers, and bit-vectors are never mixed with unbounded integers.

Division. / is real division, as in R, so x / 2 is Real even when x is an Int. %/% and %% are Z3's integer div and mod, which follow the SMT-LIB (Euclidean) convention: the remainder a %% b is always between 0 and abs(b) - 1. This agrees with R for positive divisors but differs for negative divisors: in Z3 7 %/% -2 is -3 and 7 %% -2 is 1, while R gives -4 and -1. Division by zero is not an error; Z3 treats x / 0 as an unspecified value.

Powers. x^k for a literal whole number 0 <= k <= 64 is expanded into a product and keeps the sort of x. Other powers use Z3's power operator, which is Real-valued; constraints with symbolic exponents are often beyond Z3's decision procedures and may return "unknown".

R values. An R scalar combined with a Z3 expression is converted to the sort of the other operand; see z3_int_val() for the conversion rules for doubles. Only length-one R values are accepted: z3r expressions are scalars, and R's recycling rules have no meaning for a single formula. Build several constraints with lapply() or Map().

R's own logic. && and || cannot be overloaded; use z3_and() and z3_or(). A Z3 expression is never converted to TRUE or FALSE, so if (x > 0) is an error rather than a silent mistake. Note that isTRUE() returns FALSE for any Z3 expression.

Examples

ctx <- z3_context()
x <- z3_int(ctx, "x")
y <- z3_real(ctx, "y")
p <- z3_bool(ctx, "p")
x + 1
#> <z3_expr Int> (+ x 1)
x / 2           # Real division
#> <z3_expr Real> (/ (to_real x) 2.0)
x %/% 2         # integer division
#> <z3_expr Int> (div x 2)
x^2 + y^2 <= 1
#> <z3_expr Bool> (<= (+ (to_real (* x x)) (* y y)) 1.0)
p & (x > 0) | !p
#> <z3_expr Bool> (or (and p (> x 0)) (not p))
